input.question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size
input.ground_truth: Hey there! I'm one of the bra fitting nazis over at /r/ABraThatFits, the community that produced that post you linked to, so I re-asked your question over there [and got some good answers if you want to check them out!](_URL_0_) It was super weird to see two of my favorite subreddits collide like this. Overall, however, there is not a lot of scholarship on the evolution of bras and bra sizing, which is sad, and I could probably spin you a nice little rant about sexism in academia, but I'm sure you can fill it in yourself. :) FYI, there isn't too much resistance in American brands against letters past D. No one does DDDD. Victoria's Secret goes D, DD, DDD, but lots of brands go D, DD, F, G, or D, DD, G, H. Take a look at two major US makers, Wacoal and Goddess, for examples of non-D sizing terminology. Lane Bryant, a major supplier of DD+ bras also does letters other than D. It's mostly just highly inconsistent, unlike the UK which has its stuff together.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: The history in the U.S. behind the adoption of the DD bra size

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a bunch of different-sized balloons. Some are small, some are big. People who make clothes also have to make bras in lots of different sizes, because everyone’s body is different.

Long ago, in the United States, there wasn’t a name for really big bra sizes. But some people needed bras that were much bigger than what was available. So, a company called Victoria’s Secret started using letters like D, DD, DDD, and so on, to name those bigger sizes.

The letter “D” is just a way to say “this bra is bigger than a C.” And “DD” means it’s even bigger than a D! They picked these letters because they follow the letters of the alphabet, just like how sizes go from A, B, C, and so on.

But here’s something interesting: for a long time, people didn’t talk about these bigger sizes very much because it was considered a little embarrassing. But now, more and more people are happy to have the right size and feel comfortable.

So, the “DD” bra size is just a way to help people find the right fit, like how you pick the right size shoe!
